findings.evidence: template/scripts/machine_pool.py:613–627 silently discards missing descriptors, and lines 642–647 still grant a pooled nested lease without acquiring tokens. Python subprocess calls close descriptors by default while retaining the lease environment; template/scripts/post_review_finalization.py:133–134 is one such call without pass_fds. A nested check therefore continues with no lock descriptors, and if its parent holders exit or are killed, another run can acquire all tokens while that check remains active. The nested helper in tests/test_machine_pool.py likewise invokes subprocess.run without pass_fds, so this unsupported inheritance path is explicitly accepted by the tests.
findings.summary: Nested validation can proceed without holding any pool tokens when an intermediate subprocess drops the lease descriptors.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/machine_pool.py:141–149 validates max_load_per_cpu using load <= 0, which is false for float NaN. TOML supports max_load_per_cpu = nan. The acquisition comparison load > config.max_load_per_cpu is also always false for NaN, allowing admission regardless of machine load instead of rejecting the invalid positive-number configuration.
findings.summary: A TOML NaN load limit passes validation and silently disables load admission.
